title: The Great Storm Mystery
content: Imagine a big storm with strong winds and heavy rain! Where do the birds go? Where do the dogs hide? What about you? Why don't you get wet when you are inside your house?

title: Think About It!
content: What would happen if we didn't have houses? Where would we sleep, and how would we stay safe from wild animals or cold weather?

content.title: A Shield Against the Weather
content.description: Just like an umbrella protects us from rain, a house acts like a giant umbrella and shield for our entire family.

title: What is a House?
content: A house is a building where we live with our family. It protects us from heat, cold, rain, wind, wild animals, and thieves. When we live in a house with our family, it becomes our sweet home!

definition: A building for human habitation, especially one that is lived in by a family or small group of people.

question: Why do we need a house?
options: To protect ourselves from rain, heat, and cold

title: Your Safe Place
content: Think about your favorite room in your house. Why do you like it so much? Is it because it feels cozy and safe? Imagine if you had to build a house, what would it look like?

title: Animal Homes vs. Human Homes
content: Just like we need houses, animals need homes too! A bird builds a nest, a lion lives in a den, and a rabbit digs a burrow. Every living being needs a safe place to rest and grow.

title: My Dream House Project
content: Draw a picture of your dream house. Label its different parts like the roof, windows, doors, and walls. What special room would you add to make it unique?

title: Houses that Move?
content: Have you ever seen a house that floats on water? Or a house made entirely of ice? How is that even possible?

title: Building Materials
content: If you live in a place where it rains a lot, what kind of roof should your house have? What if you travel a lot?

content.title: Building Blocks of Houses
content.description: Observe how different materials like mud, straw, bricks, cement, ice, and canvas are used to build different types of houses based on the weather and needs.

title: Different Types of Houses
content: People build different types of houses depending on where they live and the weather. Kutcha houses are made of mud and straw. Pucca houses are made of bricks and cement. There are also special houses like Igloos (made of ice), Tents (made of canvas), and Houseboats (floating houses).

definition: A dome-shaped Eskimo house, typically built from blocks of solid snow.

content: Encourage students to discuss what their houses are made of. This brings the concept closer to their daily lives.
Students often think igloos are cold inside. Explain that the ice blocks actually trap body heat and keep the inside warm!

question: Which type of house is made of solid snow?

title: Your House
content: Look at your own house. Is it a Kutcha house or a Pucca house? What materials do you think were used to build it?

title: Geography and Homes
content: The type of house depends on geography! In places with heavy snow, roofs are sloped so the snow slides off. In deserts, houses have thick walls to keep the inside cool.

title: Match the Materials
content: Look around your neighborhood. Can you find 3 different materials used in building houses? Write them down and guess why they were used.
